title: Outcome contract v1
description: The one project record for the estate (2026-09-08 debate judgment): Intake V2 writes it, the door checks it before planning, Daybook reads it. Amended after the 2026-09-08 Opus adversarial review (F1 to F12). Only the keyword subset scripts/contract_check.py actually enforces is used here: type, required, properties, enum, const, items, minItems, additionalProperties. The custom top level key x-question-pivot names the state literal the questions cap treats as its lower bound, so that literal is read from the schema rather than hard coded a second time in the checker (F5). Rules the keyword subset cannot express, named here and enforced by hand in contract_check.py so a reader of either file finds the same account: (1) question and language must be non-empty after stripping whitespace; (2) ticket is required (non-null) when audit.required is true; (3) questions holds at most one entry once state is at or past x-question-pivot (contracted), and none once state is delivered or later (the A-prime rule, refined by F12); (4) every field of the project object (not persona, language, question or the rest, which come from the ask itself and carry no provenance, F6) must have a provenance entry, and every provenance entry must name a real project field (F7); (5) once state is delivered or later, every must_answer entry needs a non-empty answer and a receipt_id that names a real entry in receipts (F1); (6) every receipts[].ref must start with file:, evidence: or url:, the grammar scripts/receipt_check.py resolves (F4); (7) every success_checks entry whose expect is contains or file-exists needs a non-empty value (F9); (8) success_checks may be empty only while state is draft, and at least one entry is required once state is at or past x-question-pivot (contracted), reading the same pivot the questions cap reads rather than a second hard coded literal. The decision field (object or null) points at the intake decision JSON that decide.py scores; it never copies that record's options, criteria or weights in here, so the decision JSON stays the single ranking (F2).

schema_version.description: Which shape this record follows, so a reader never has to guess.

project.description: The project this record is about, and where each fact about it came from. Provenance binds this object's fields only (F6): persona, language, question and the rest of the top level record come from the ask itself and carry no provenance entry.

project_id.description: A stable identifier for the project.

repository.description: Where the project's code lives, each field a string or the literal NO-DATA when it could not be determined.

branch.description: The branch this record was raised against, or NO-DATA.

remote.description: The git remote URL, or NO-DATA.

provenance.description: Maps every project field name present above (project_id, name, repository) to where it came from, and names no field that is not one of them (checked by hand in both directions, F7).

language.description: The language the user wrote in, BCP 47 style (en, ja, fr). Carries no provenance entry: it comes from the ask itself (F6).

question.description: The exact ask, verbatim. Must not be empty after stripping whitespace (enforced by hand, since the enforced keyword subset carries no minLength). Carries no provenance entry: it comes from the ask itself (F6).

success_checks.description: Runnable checks that prove the outcome landed. May be empty only while state is draft; once state is at or past the schema's own x-question-pivot (contracted), at least one entry is required (enforced by hand, since the enforced keyword subset has no conditional-by-sibling-value minItems).

id.description: A short identifier for this check.

expect.description: How the command's result is read.

value.description: The expected text or path. Required and non-empty when expect is contains or file-exists (enforced by hand, since the enforced keyword subset has no conditional-by-sibling-value requirement, F9).

must_answer.description: Open fields that must be answered before this contract is complete. May be empty, but the key is always present. Once state is delivered or later, every entry needs a non-empty answer and a receipt_id naming a real entry in receipts (enforced by hand, F1).

answer.description: The answer given for this field, or null when not yet answered.

receipt_id.description: The id of the receipts[] entry that backs the answer, or null when not yet cited.

affected_products.description: Which of this estate's products the outcome touches.

ticket.description: The tracking ticket, or null when none is filed yet. Required (non-null) when audit.required is true: a conditional the enforced keyword subset cannot express, so contract_check.py enforces it by hand rather than inventing a new keyword here.

id.description: The ticket's id in that system.

audit.description: Whether this outcome needs an audit trail, and where its manifest lives.

required.description: Whether an audit manifest is mandatory for this record.

manifest.description: Path to the audit manifest, or null when audit.required is false.

persona.description: The persona this outcome is written for: one of Intake V2's three personas, or the literal NO-DATA when unknown. Carries no provenance entry: it comes from the ask itself (F6).

state.description: Where this record sits in its own lifecycle. Daybook v2 derives four DISPLAY columns from this and from decision, never storing them: open (draft/contracted/planned/in-flight with decision null or decision.close_call false), close-call (decision.close_call true, not delivered, not superseded), decided (delivered), superseded (superseded). See docs/schema/README.md, 'State and the Daybook columns' (F3).

receipts.description: Evidence gathered so far. May be empty, but the key is always present.

id.description: A short identifier for this receipt.

path.description: Where the full evidence lives, a human readable copy of the location ref resolves.

ref.description: The resolver grammar scripts/receipt_check.py understands: file:<path>:<start>-<end>, evidence:<name>, or url:<u>. Must start with one of those three prefixes (enforced by hand, since the enforced keyword subset has no pattern keyword, F4).

questions.description: Blocking questions still open for a person to answer. May be empty, but the key is always present. At most one entry is allowed once state is at or past x-question-pivot (contracted), and none once state is delivered or later (the A-prime rule, refined by F12): a cross-field count the enforced keyword subset cannot express, so contract_check.py enforces it by hand.

field.description: The field the question is about.

history.description: Stamps of what happened to this record over time. May be empty, but the key is always present.

by.description: Who or what made it happen (git, manifest, readme, ask, answer).

decision.description: The weighed decision behind this record, or null when no weighed decision has happened yet. Points at the intake decision JSON that decide.py scores; never copies that record's options, criteria or weights into this contract, so the decision JSON stays the single ranking (F2).

record.description: Path to the intake decision JSON that decide.py scores.

close_call.description: Whether decide.py judged this a close call.

margin.description: The margin decide.py computed between the top two options, or null when not scored.

chosen.description: The id of the option decide.py chose, or null when not scored.
